briefing.headline: OpenAI and xAI accelerate frontier model releases as US-China compute race intensifies.

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The global AI race has entered a high-stakes phase with multiple frontier labs shipping advanced reasoning models. Funding remains robust while regulatory scrutiny grows over deployment risks. Multi-agent systems are emerging as the next capability frontier.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released o4-preview with improved long-horizon planning. Anthropic's Claude 4 Opus and Google's Gemini 3.0 Ultra both launched this month. Meta open-sourced Llama 4 while xAI deployed Grok-3 on its Memphis supercluster.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New NIST guidelines emphasize runtime monitoring for agentic workflows.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: TSMC began volume production of 1.6nm AI chips. Microsoft announced a $15B data center expansion in Texas. Saudi Arabia committed $8B to a sovereign AI compute cluster.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will multi-agent coordination protocols become standardized before the first superintelligent system emerges?
